title: Se pasivo: los movimientos de independencia

sections.content: The se-passive treats the wars of independence as a collective phenomenon: uprisings were organized, a conflict was waged, campaigns were carried out, an army was defeated — without crediting a single leader for something that was, in practice, thousands of people's doing. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En México se libró un conflicto casi ininterrumpido entre 1810 y 1821.
items.english: In Mexico, an almost uninterrupted conflict was waged between 1810 and 1821.

items.spanish: Se organizaron levantamientos contra las autoridades coloniales en distintos momentos y lugares.
items.english: Uprisings against colonial authorities were organized at different times and places.

items.spanish: En Sudamérica se llevaron a cabo campañas militares enormes a lo largo de miles de kilómetros.
items.english: In South America, enormous military campaigns were carried out across thousands of kilometers.

items.spanish: En la batalla de Ayacucho se derrotó de manera decisiva al último gran ejército realista del continente.
items.english: At the Battle of Ayacucho, the continent's last great royalist army was decisively defeated.

sections.content: Llevarse a cabo (to be carried out) is a set phrase almost always used in the se-passive or the ordinary passive — you'll rarely see it any other way, which makes it a useful chunk to memorize whole rather than building word by word.
